summary: Magnum Photos is an international photographic cooperative founded in 1947 by major photojournalists, owned by its photographer-members who retain copyrights to their work. It is known for its vast archive and a three-stage membership system. The cooperative faced controversy in 2020 over archive content, leading to the suspension and resignation of photographer David Alan Harvey.

claims.text: Magnum Photos is an international photographic cooperative owned by its photographer-members.
claims.evidence_quote: Magnum Photos is an international photographic cooperative owned by its photographer-members, with offices in Paris, New York City and London.

claims.text: It was founded in 1947 in Paris by Robert Capa, David Seymour, Maria Eisner, Henri Cartier-Bresson, George Rodger, William Vandivert, and Rita Vandivert.
claims.evidence_quote: It was founded in 1947 in Paris by photographers Robert Capa, David "Chim" Seymour, Maria Eisner, Henri Cartier-Bresson, George Rodger, William Vandivert, and Rita Vandivert.

claims.text: Magnum photographers retain all copyrights to their own work.
claims.evidence_quote: Its photographers retain all copyrights to their own work.

claims.text: Rita Vandivert was the cooperative's first president and head of the New York office, while Maria Eisner headed the Paris office.
claims.evidence_quote: Rita Vandivert was the cooperative's first president and head of the New York office, while Maria Eisner headed the Paris office.

claims.text: In 1955, Magnum set up a three-stage membership system that continues to this day.
claims.evidence_quote: However, in 1955 a three-stage membership system was set up that continues to this day

claims.text: Magnum's photographers meet once a year during the last weekend in June in New York City, Paris or London.
claims.evidence_quote: Magnum's photographers meet once a year, during the last weekend in June, in New York City, Paris or London, to discuss the cooperative's business.

claims.text: The Magnum digital archive contains more than 1 million images.
claims.evidence_quote: Magnum Photos' digital archive constitutes more than 1 million images, which Magnum licenses through its website.

claims.text: In 2010, MSD Capital acquired nearly 200,000 original press prints of Magnum photographers, donating them to the Harry Ransom Center in 2013.
claims.evidence_quote: In 2010, MSD Capital acquired a collection of nearly 200,000 original press prints of images taken by Magnum photographers, which in 2013 it donated to the Harry Ransom Center.

claims.text: In August 2020, the Magnum website was taken offline after concerns were raised about photographs of children in the archive.
claims.evidence_quote: In August 2020, the Magnum website was taken offline after issues were raised by the Fstoppers photography website and amplified on social media by others including Jörg Colberg.

claims.text: Much of the criticism focused on David Alan Harvey's photographs of sex workers in Bangkok in 1989.
claims.evidence_quote: Much of the criticism [...] has focused on a series of photographs by the US photographer David Alan Harvey from his time documenting sex workers in Bangkok in 1989.

claims.text: David Alan Harvey was suspended for a year after a formal investigation into sexual misconduct allegations, then resigned in 2021.
claims.evidence_quote: Harvey was later suspended for a year following a formal investigation into sexual misconduct allegations against him.

claims.text: Magnum voted to remove David Alan Harvey as a member and he resigned in 2021 before the board's final meeting.
claims.evidence_quote: Magnum voted to remove him as a member and he resigned in 2021 before the board had their final meeting regarding the matter.
